text: We evaluated aggressive gradient clipping during student fine-tuning (clip_norm 0.5) in a weak-to-strong setup where a qwen2.5-0.5b weak supervisor, with weak_acc 0.65, trains a qwen2.5-3b student whose own ceiling performance is strong_acc 0.91. Across num_seeds 3 seeds, the clipped student reached transfer_acc 0.79 (transfer_acc_se 0.01) and a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.54 with pgr_se 0.03, against a baseline_pgr of 0.53. The difference between the measured PGR and the baseline falls well within two standard errors of the estimate, so these data do not support a claim that clipping improves generalization from weak supervision; the outcome is best read as indistinguishable from the baseline at this sample size. With only three seeds, the standard errors are themselves loosely estimated, and no variance figure is available for the baseline, which further limits comparison. Replication with more seeds and a range of clip_norm values would be needed before drawing conclusions about the method's effect.
